### What `docs/AMD_HIP_PERFORMANCE.md` does

This document is the performance and reproducibility companion to `docs/AMD_HIP.md`. While `AMD_HIP.md` explains how to install and build the experimental AMD HIP backend, `AMD_HIP_PERFORMANCE.md` records the exact configuration, environment variables, and benchmark methodology used to produce the performance numbers cited elsewhere in the project. It is intended for users who want to reproduce the measured results or understand the precise conditions under which the HIP backend was validated.

The file begins by stating that this opt-in Linux `gfx1100` backend supersedes the initial support in PR #94. It lists the retained features (HIP runtime, wave32 integer-dot compatibility, native mmap layout validation, MTP) and the additions (HIP MMQ, optional calibrated dense hipBLASLt GEMM, native prefill batching, host-memory/SSD paths, and a reusable pinned staging buffer for blocking expert uploads).
